reason: The text describes a coordinated effort between leaders and people. Moses commands Joshua to choose men and fight Amalek; Joshua obeys this command and leads the people in battle. Simultaneously, Moses, Aaron, and Hur work together on the hill—Aaron and Hur explicitly support Moses' hands as he holds up the rod of God (וַתָּֽמְכ֣וּ בְיָדָ֗יו). The account shows that Israel's victory depends on this combined effort: Joshua and the people execute the fighting while the leaders provide spiritual support, with the text indicating that when Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed. This demonstrates a hierarchical but coordinated working relationship between leadership and the broader community.
